title: Port windows are a fractional Haemers bound: w >= 53/6 on P104 (no new κ)
body:
## Result

No new κ and no word. The package `research/p104-port-window-haemers` is a proof note on the window w = rank/k of a k-block mask pattern on the ports (B_ST = 0 on orthogonal pairs, B_TT invertible). Statements, proofs and a hypothesis ledger are in `THEOREM.md`.

1. **The window is the fractional Haemers bound.** With G the odd graph on the ports (distinct ports adjacent when their F_2 dot product is 1), the pattern with identity diagonal blocks is word for word a d-representation of G in the sense of Bukh and Cox (IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory 65 (2019) 3340-3348, arXiv:1802.00476, Section 2), so w = H_f(G; F); at k = 1 it is Haemers' bound (IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory 25 (1979) 231-232). The parameter is due to Blasiak's thesis (Cornell, 2013), as cited by Bukh and Cox.
2. **Floor on P104.** For an orthogonal 8-set K with 22 edge ports of degrees (5,5,5,5,6,6,6,6) (960 of the 1728 orthogonal 8-sets of P104), a weighted star bound gives rank >= 8k + 5k/6 for every k-block pattern over every field, so **w(P104; F) >= 53/6**, and rank >= 9k for k <= 5. In particular no k = 2 pattern of rank 17, no k = 3 pattern of rank 26 and no k = 4 pattern of rank 34 exist.
3. **P112 and P120.** The same theorem gives rank >= 9k, and the F_2 Gram matrix has rank 9, so w = 9 exactly in characteristic 2 on both (P112 is P104 plus one of the two odd 8-cliques that P120 deletes). In characteristic not 2, w >= 13 on P104 (14 on P112, 15 on P120), from the Hadamard product with the Gram matrix of the E8 root lines.
4. **Exact data at k = 2.** A 14-port subset of P104 has a 2-block pattern of rank 17 < 18 = 9k, exact over Q, F_2 and F_3 (150 forced-zero pairs, 0 violations): rank >= 9k fails on subsets. The 104-port formula "rank <= 17 at k = 2 over F_2" is UNSAT with a DRAT proof (`data/full_k2_rank17_f2.drat.xz`, 25.7 MB uncompressed) that drat-trim verified in forward mode; kissat 4.0.4 found the formula UNSAT in 7 s, with the same formula SAT at rank 18 and the 14-port formula SAT at 17 and UNSAT at 16. Theorem 3 gives the same fact over every field, so this is a cross-check of the encoding.
5. **Tensor windows.** A tensor lift of width f has rank 9f (ratio 9), and on a tensor window the decoder price satisfies c_k >= k c_1.

Widening the integer window to the rational rank/k is the concept-stretching step of Lakatos, *Proofs and Refutations* (1976); the 14-port subset is the local counterexample to "rank >= 9k".

## What is open

w(P104; F_2) is in [53/6, 9]; the first block size not excluded by the floor is k = 6, rank 53. The proof uses 30 of the 104 ports. Odd characteristic has lower bounds only. A window below 9 needs a block representation that is not a tensor lift; none is constructed here.

## Checks

`check.py` (about 15 s) and `check_sat.py` (a few seconds), standard library only, from the package: the system counts (960 + 384 + 384 types, 1728, 4032 and 8640 orthogonal 8-sets), the weights and exact bounds (5/6, 101/126, 3/4; 1 on P112 and P120), the floor table, the 14-port pattern over Q, F_2, F_3, every inequality of the proof on explicit representations, the E8 map, regeneration of the five DIMACS formulas with counts and sha256, and failing controls (planted violations, weights outside the hypotheses, a non-tensor window, mutated labellings). The solver and proof-checker runs are recorded, not repeated by the checks. The registered-package validator passes on a scratch copy at base 7c49fe32c.

## Not claimed

No bound on κ; nothing priced. The window is defined by the block mask, and its physical realisation for k > 1 is not derived. Weights are from a grid and not claimed optimal. No human has reviewed the proofs; Theorem 3 and the odd-characteristic argument were re-derived by a second model session.
